items.fullSentence: Je mange toujours du riz le soir.
items.sentenceTrans: I always eat rice in the evening.

whyWrong.parfois: That means 'sometimes', but the sentence says 'always'.
whyWrong.jamais: That means 'never' and needs 'ne'; the meaning here is 'always'.
whyWrong.souvent: That means 'often', but the sentence says 'always'.

items.fullSentence: Nous mangeons parfois du gâteau le week-end.
items.sentenceTrans: We sometimes eat cake at the weekend.

whyWrong.souvent: That means 'often', but the sentence says 'sometimes'.
whyWrong.parfois de: parfois is a complete adverb — no 'de' follows it here.
whyWrong.quelque fois: The adverb is one word, quelquefois (or parfois) — not 'quelque fois'.

items.fullSentence: Je mange rarement de la restauration rapide.

whyWrong.rares: rares is a plural adjective — to modify the verb you need the adverb rarement.
whyWrong.très rare: rare is an adjective ('rare'); the adverb is rarement.
whyWrong.rare: That's the adjective; you need the adverb rarement to modify the verb.

items.fullSentence: Elle ne mange jamais de sucre.

whyWrong.pas jamais: Use only one negative word — ne...jamais.

items.fullSentence: Je bois du café tous les jours.

whyWrong.tout les jours: tout must agree — the masculine plural is tous.
whyWrong.toutes les jours: jour is masculine — tous, not toutes.
whyWrong.chaque les jours: chaque is singular and takes no article — say chaque jour or tous les jours.

items.fullSentence: On mange au restaurant de temps en temps.
items.sentenceTrans: We eat out from time to time.

whyWrong.des temps en temps: The fixed phrase uses de, not des.
whyWrong.de temps à temps: The set expression is 'de temps en temps' (or de temps à autre).
whyWrong.du temps en temps: The fixed phrase starts with de, not du.

items.fullSentence: Elle mange souvent de la salade au déjeuner.
items.sentenceTrans: She often eats salad at lunch.

whyWrong.souvent de: The adverb stands alone — de la salade already has its article.
